script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Good morning, FitZone gym. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Hi, I'd like to join. Are there any special prices for students?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Yes, students get a discount. The student membership is thirty pounds a month, and the standard one is forty-five.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: Great, I'll take the student one. Do I need to bring anything?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Please bring your student card and a form of photo ID. Also, the pool is only open until eight in the evening, but the gym stays open until ten.

script.speaker: Customer
script.text: That's fine. My name is Daniel Brooks, and I'd like to start on Monday.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Perfect, Daniel. I'll book your induction for Monday at ten o'clock.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Welcome to Northfield University. I'll show you the main places you will need during your first week. First, the library is on your left. It has four floors, and the silent study area is on the top floor. Borrowing is free, and you can keep a book for four weeks.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Next, the student centre. This is where you collect your timetable and ID card. It is open from eight thirty to five, Monday to Friday. If you have questions about accommodation, go to room twelve on the ground floor.

script.speaker: Guide
script.text: Finally, the sports hall is behind the main building. Registration for clubs happens on Thursday afternoon, and the most popular clubs, such as basketball and photography, fill up quickly, so arrive early.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Today I'd like to talk about the relationship between sleep and memory. For a long time, people assumed that sleep was simply a period of rest for the brain. Research over the past few decades suggests something rather different.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: In one well-known type of experiment, participants learn a list of words and are then divided into two groups. One group sleeps for eight hours, while the other stays awake. When tested later, the group that slept usually remembers more words.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: Scientists believe that during deep sleep the brain replays recent experiences, which helps move information from short-term to long-term storage. It is worth stressing, however, that the effect varies between individuals, and that sleeping longer does not always lead to better results.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.text: For students, the practical message is fairly clear: studying late into the night at the expense of sleep is unlikely to be an effective strategy.
